subject: MAP: Performance benchmark — tooling mismatch root-cause and repro plan
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tim Jenkins <tim.jenkins@acme.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: Performance benchmark — tooling mismatch root-cause and repro plan

Hi Tim —

Thanks again for running the initial set of tests last week. We reviewed the runs you shared and ran a parallel set from our side using the MAP test harness. The headline: latency (TTFT) and concurrency behavior diverge under sustained load — your numbers show ~2.1s median TTFT at 8 concurrent streams vs our ~1.2s, and throughput drops earlier on your runs.

Preliminary triage highlights three likely contributors:
- Tooling difference: your team used "FortressBench" v1.4 with the default batching and short prefix padding; our internal harness uses continuous-batching + warmed KV cache with explicit stream prefetch.
- Model artifact: you ran the quantized variant (q4_0) while our baseline is fp16; quantization and kernel selection change the per-token runtime characteristics and cache hit patterns.
- Warmup/kv-cache: our production runs explicitly warm the KV cache and reuse session context; cold-session runs inflates TTFT in early tokens.

Proposal (short):
1) Reproduce your exact run on our infra (we will run using FortressBench flags you provided) — owner: Soojin — target: 48 hours.
2) Run a matched configuration where we align model artifact (q4_0) and batching parameters you used — owner: Soojin — target: 48–72 hours.
3) Canary re-run with recommended settings (warm cache, continuous batching, streaming enabled) so we can show the delta in TTFT and throughput inside the MAP — owner: Marissa/Karthik — target: business-day after repro results.

Attachments: redwood_map_v2_benchmark_results.xlsx (summary + per-run traces), ttft_trace_logs.zip (sample token-level traces). I also linked the MAP runbook in Drive for procedure alignment.

Ask: please confirm availability for a 30m call Thu or Fri to align on the repro flags and agree on a canary window. If you can send the exact FortressBench CLI flags and the artifact checksum you used that will speed repro.

Thanks —
Marissa
Marissa Cole | Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192

From: Tim Jenkins <tim.jenkins@acme.com>

Cc: Acme Systems Engineering <eng-team@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 09:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: Performance benchmark — tooling mismatch root-cause and repro plan

Thanks Marissa —

Appreciate the breakdown. Confirming we used FortressBench v1.4 (default batch size 4, pad-to-max-token disabled), model artifact label: acme-q4_0-20270712 (sha256: 8f3d...), and we did not perform explicit KV warmup in these runs. Our engineering lead Jon made a note that their harness streams tokens differently (buffer every 32 tokens then flush).

We'll prioritize sending the exact CLI flags and a short run manifest by EOD. We can do a quick sync on Friday 10:00am PT — Jon (eng lead) and I will join.

- Tim
Tim Jenkins | Staff ML Engineer | Acme Systems
tim.jenkins@acme.com | +1 206-555-0147

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Tim Jenkins <tim.jenkins@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: Performance benchmark — tooling mismatch root-cause and repro plan

Marissa / Tim —

I'm starting the repro now. A couple of technical clarifications that will affect parity:
1) Tokenization: does the FortressBench config use the same tokenizer (BPE variant) and truncation policy? Small differences in pre-tokenization can change token counts and thus per-token timing.
2) Concurrency pattern: can you share whether your 8 concurrent streams are long-lived connections (session reuse) or short-running independent calls?
3) RNG / sampling: were any non-deterministic sampling params used in those runs (top_k/top_p/temperature) or were they greedy?

If you can confirm those three things I will run (a) exact parity reproduction on our infra using your flags, and (b) a matched-run where we keep everything equal but swap model artifact to our fp16 baseline so we can isolate quantization impact. I will capture token-level traces and a TTFT distribution.

Soojin

soojin_lee@redwood.ai

Thanks all — quick status and action-item MAP update (attached updated MAP sheet):

Action items (owners / due):
- Soojin: reproduce Acme FortressBench v1.4 run on Redwood infra and deliver per-token trace + TTFT distribution (due 2027-08-06 17:00 PT) — attachment: ttft_trace_logs.zip
- Tim / Acme: confirm tokenizer/truncation and whether streams are long-lived (reply by 2027-08-05 17:00 PT) — Tim acknowledged (see earlier reply)
- Marissa / Karthik: schedule canary window and notify procurement; prepare SOW amendment if we push close date (draft due 2027-08-07)

If Soojin's parity run reproduces your numbers we will run the matched artifact test next to isolate quantization impact. If parity does not reproduce, we will start a tooling-delta checklist (padding, buffering, flush interval, tokenization) and run a side-by-side head-to-head.

Friday 10:00am PT is confirmed for the 30m sync (Marissa, Karthik, Soojin, Tim, Jon). I'll circulate a calendar invite with an agenda and a short runbook excerpt we plan to execute during the canary.

Marissa
